nodes.label: Moriarty
nodes.rationale: Experimental language and toolchain so developers can describe financial state, permitted actions, payment obligations and authorization rules, then compile those descriptions into Compact with a proof that execution and contract history satisfy the agreement.

nodes.label: Midnight Preview
nodes.rationale: Hard acceptance gate: each supported financial capability needs Preview execution, retained transaction IDs, finalized native effects and state readback checked against language semantics. Local tests and compiled artifacts support that evidence but do not close the network gate.

nodes.label: Compact
nodes.rationale: Compact supports Midnight contracts and zero-knowledge circuits; Moriarty adds financial-operation rules Compact does not express (asset denomination, interest rounding, due dates, authorization, surviving obligations).

nodes.label: ACTUS
nodes.rationale: Algorithmic Contract Types Unified Standards supply reference behavior for events, state transitions and cash flows. Moriarty must reproduce relevant financial behavior including dates and rounding; naming a contract type is not enough.

nodes.label: DeFi Kernel Study
nodes.rationale: Project catalogue of decentralized-finance behaviors (swaps, liquidity, lending, composition). Supplies implementation and conformance requirements; applications do not connect to it as a runtime service.

nodes.label: Marlowe
nodes.rationale: Financial-contract DSL designed to make contract behavior amenable to analysis. Moriarty adopts the goal of reasoning about an agreement before execution and is developing authoring, proof and settlement architecture for Midnight.

nodes.label: EBNF
nodes.rationale: Moriarty selects EBNF (ISO/IEC 14977) for its source grammar because it extends BNF with repetition and optionality. EBNF describes the grammar; it does not decide whether source resembles Lisp or a language with braces. ABNF RFC 5234 is acknowledged as another BNF-family notation used for protocols but is not selected.

nodes.label: K Framework
nodes.rationale: Selected framework for Moriarty's formal operational semantics. Describes execution through configurations and rewrite rules. Typing judgments define admissible programs; denotational models can support particular financial analyses but do not replace the execution definition.

nodes.label: moriarty-bounded-atomic/1
nodes.rationale: Existing atomic grammar and TypeScript evaluator profile. Loan, swap and Compact workflow in the README use this profile; profiles are not interchangeable.

nodes.label: moriarty-funded-source/0
nodes.rationale: Uses older successor-syntax/0 header and grammar through a separate preparation API. Supports a typed subset with Transfer and Repay emissions producing local Prepared candidates. Rejects state/const, requires, let, next, ensures, projections and operators even though those forms appear in the expression grammar. Numeric values limited to UInt128. Parsing or local preparation does not establish authorization, proof, ledger acceptance or source/Core/K correspondence.

nodes.label: Executable Expression Runtime
nodes.rationale: Implements all 40 Core constructors; checks types before execution, uses exact integer arithmetic, evaluates Boolean branches selectively and publishes no tentative state after rejection.

nodes.label: Financial Expression Runtime
nodes.rationale: Adds eight pure constructors in a separate versioned API. Original expression profile remains unchanged. Vault conversion cases exercise deposit, mint, withdrawal and redemption arithmetic; they do not execute those financial actions or establish ledger acceptance.

nodes.label: Felleisen-Hieb Reduction Semantics
nodes.rationale: Presentation method for the implemented repayment subset: terms, evaluation contexts, primitive contractions, context closure and terminal answers. Felleisen and Hieb Revised Report §2 Definitions 2.1/2.3 and §3.1 supplies the presentation method; its metatheorems are not claims about Moriarty.

nodes.label: Prepared
nodes.rationale: Local proposal produced by K/codec, not authorization or Midnight acceptance.

nodes.label: Turing Incompleteness
nodes.rationale: Current language has no loop construct or source recursion. Registered profile bounds values, intermediate arithmetic, expression depth, collection sizes, work per action, contract lifetime and time horizon. These limits make termination and resource obligations explicit; they do not automatically prove financial correctness, practical proving cost or that a proof fits a particular circuit. Execution limits do not cancel financial obligations.

nodes.label: Registered Bounds Document
nodes.rationale: Frontend admits the exact registered bounds.json by content hash; editing its limits or even reformatting its JSON is not a supported configuration change.

nodes.label: Effect
nodes.rationale: Records an action's financial result (transfer, fee, newly created due or settlement of a due). Recording an effect in the simulator does not move ledger assets.

nodes.label: Exact Plan
nodes.rationale: Authorization form that fixes the action, state writes and effects a participant authorizes. Distinct from outcome intents. Exact-plan signatures may additionally bind the selected execution.

nodes.label: Outcome Intent
nodes.rationale: Authorization form that permits a plan to be chosen within constraints: maximum gross spending, minimum net receipts, allowed actions, recipients and calls. Refunds do not erase gross spending; fees count when checking net receipts.

nodes.label: Core
nodes.rationale: Compiler's explicit representation of the agreement's operations. Source locations, semantic versions, canonical encodings and hashes connect it to the source and registered bounds. Compiler and evaluator share this typed representation.

nodes.label: Local Simulation
nodes.rationale: Simulation does not sign, prove, submit or consume a ledger state. The acceptance entry point rejects without its required backend.

nodes.label: Compact Mapper
nodes.rationale: Translates a restricted subset into pure Compact execution kernels with no persistent ledger declarations or witness functions. Circuits constrain arithmetic hints; supplying a quotient or multiplication limb does not make it trusted. Test wrappers store results for comparison; they do not move assets or implement the full acceptance protocol.

nodes.label: Proof-Carrying Data
nodes.rationale: A piece of data carries evidence that it was produced according to specified rules, including validity of predecessor data. For Moriarty that data is a contract transition. Recursive proofs check predecessor proofs inside a new proof; recursion in the proof system does not add unbounded recursion to the source language. A valid history proof does not establish that an external price is true or that a previous state has not already been spent. Zero-knowledge capability does not by itself provide private witness handoff. Enforcement in the ledger acceptance path remains unimplemented.

nodes.label: Native IVC Experiment
nodes.rationale: Uses Midnight's Halo2-based IVC backend. Prepared encoding constrains a fixed loan scenario to known states; it does not yet prove the general Moriarty transition relation. Connecting its complete verifier to Midnight's ledger verifier is an unresolved engineering boundary; a host-computed verification flag cannot substitute. The project has not yet produced a native recursive Moriarty proof.

nodes.label: Browser Developer Mock
nodes.rationale: Explores proposed user flows with simulated authority and certificates; it is a separate prototype, not a browser frontend for the source compiler.

nodes.label: Expression-Source Bounds
nodes.rationale: Parser limits (65536 source bytes, 8192 tokens, AST 8192, depth 64, etc.) are separate from atomic execution bounds and from financial runtime limits. Syntax acceptance does not imply execution.

nodes.label: ABORT Rule
nodes.rationale: ABORT discards the entire continuation, including finalization; rejected output has no tentative state or effects.
